chunks: Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who ordered his slave to kill a man, and he killed him: 'And is the slave of a man anything but like his whip or like his sword? The master is executed because of it, and the slave is placed in prison.'

key_terms.السَّيِّد: The master/owner — bears full legal liability for ordering the killing
key_terms.الْعَبْد: The slave — treated as an instrument; imprisoned but not executed
key_terms.كَسَوْطِهِ أَوْ كَسَيْفِهِ: Like his whip or sword — metaphor establishing the slave as a mere instrument of the master's will
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: Executed (qisas/retaliation) — the master faces capital punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when a master orders his slave to commit murder?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a ruling from Imam Ali (AS) on criminal liability when a master commands his slave to commit murder. Imam Ali's ruling establishes that the master bears full capital liability — because the slave, lacking independent legal agency, is treated as an instrument (like a whip or sword). The slave, who carried out the act, is imprisoned but not executed. This ruling illustrates the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that coerced agents do not bear the same liability as the one who exercises the directing will.
